doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sixties: Verve end, California, Half Note, Duets
title: Return to Tristano and the 1964 'Look Up and Live' broadcast
summary: He returned for the last time at the Half Note and discusses the broadcast and the band's end.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So basically after a couple years out there Lennie calls you and you finally get back and he puts together the quintet with Warne, Sonny Dallas, and Nick Stabulas right? That’s the band that’s on the “Look up and Live” broadcast.
That’s sixty-four, that broadcast?
Yeah.
Okay.
Which is now on you tube. You can see a lot of it on you tube. I tell my students to go look at that because that’s the one chance you get to see the old Half Note. The legendary old Half Note.
And hear Lennie playing great.
Yeah, and everybody playing great.
I don’t think I was visible in that.
You were.
I was off to the side kind of in the dark. You could see kind of a silhouette.
You could see a [profile], yeah, kind of a silhouette. You’re not totally invisible. You’re not in full profile to be sure.
That was kind of a nice presentation. The religious connection made some sense the way the man talked about it.
You did some other gigs at the time with that band correct? A handful anyway.
In sixty-four?
Yeah.
I thought that was the last one.
Okay. There were no others other than the Half Note?
I’m not sure.
But at that point the band basically fell apart or Lennie didn’t want to continue or what happened?
I don’t really know why it broke up.
But it did?
Yeah. I was thinking I had moved to Europe but I really hadn’t permanently then or semi-permanently.
